id: title:Gilbert09:treat max connections per hour resource limit as non retryable

review.posthog_relevance: Adds MySQL error 1226 to the set of non-retryable database connection errors, preventing warehouse ingestion jobs from entering a retry loop when the database user hits its hourly connection quota.
review.reason: Adds MySQL error 1226 to the set of non-retryable database connection errors, preventing warehouse ingestion jobs from entering a retry loop when the database user hits its hourly connection quota.
review.uncertainty: The benefit relies on the existence of this specific MySQL configuration and the operational workflow of warehouse ingestion; while the code change is substantive and bounded, the actual prevention of a retry loop and its impact on warehouse ingestion is not independently verified.

observations.limitations: Only supplied hunk IDs are cited. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds MySQL error 1226 (ER_USER_LIMIT_REACHED) to the set of non-retryable connection errors, with a comment explaining that the resource limit resets hourly and immediate retries do not help.
observations.code_quote: "(1226,": "Your MySQL/MariaDB user account has a 'max_connections_per_hour' resource limit configured, and PostHog has used it up for this hour (error 1226). The limit resets at the top of the next hour, but retrying now only spends more of that quota. Ask your database admin to raise or remove the limit on the connecting user, then resync.",
observations.posthog_connection: This change prevents PostHog warehouse ingestion jobs from entering a retry loop when the database user hits its hourly connection quota, directing users to contact their DB admin instead.

observations.behavior: Adds a test case asserting that MySQL error 1226 messages are recognized as non-retryable, covering both raw pymysql and Temporal-wrapped string representations.
